before.stem: Ww Regarding the glossopharyngeal nerve, which of the following statements is INCORRECT:
options: The glossopharyngeal nerve originates from the medulla. 4% (x) The glossopharyngeal nerve emerges from the cranial cavity via the jugular foramen. 4%

The glossopharyngeal nerve innervates the stylopharyngeus muscle.

after.stem: Regarding the glossopharyngeal nerve, which of the following statements is INCORRECT:
options: The glossopharyngeal nerve originates from the medulla.
The glossopharyngeal nerve emerges from the cranial cavity via the jugular foramen.
The glossopharyngeal nerve is the efferent nerve of the gag reflex.
The glossopharyngeal nerve innervates the stylopharyngeus muscle.
The glossopharyngeal nerve supplies parasympathetic fibres to the parotid gland.

before.stem: A 54 year old man presents to ED complaining of difficulty chewing. On examination, you note he has loss of muscle bulk over the masseter muscle and loss of power opening the jaw. He also has loss of tactile sensation involving the anterior two thirds of the tongue. Which of the following cranial nerves is most likely affected:
warnings: No marked correct option was detected.
before.explanation: The muscles of mastication are innervated by the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve, which also supplies tactile sensation to the anterior two-thirds of the tongue. The glossopharyngeal nerve supplies taste and general sensation to the posterior third of the tongue. The chorda tympani branch of the facial nerve supplies taste to the anterior two-thirds of the tongue. Vv

before.stem: Regarding the oculomotor nerve, which of the following statements is CORRECT:
options: The oculomotor nerve has both motor and sensory function.
The oculomotor nerve innervates all of the extraocular muscles. ie The oculomotor ne! rve innervates the dilator pupillae muscle. 23%
The oculomotor nerve passes through the lateral part of the cavernous sinus.
The oculomotor nerve enters the orbit through the optic canal.
before.explanation: The oculomotor nerve does travel through the lateral aspect of the cavernous sinus, together with CN IV and VI nerves and the ophthalmic division of CN V. It enters the orbit through the superior orbital fissure. It innervates only four out of six of the extraocular muscles, in addition to the sphincter pupillae muscle. The oculomotor nerve is a pure motor nerve; it has no sensory function. Vv

after.stem: Regarding the oculomotor nerve, which of the following statements is CORRECT:
options: The oculomotor nerve has both motor and sensory function.
The oculomotor nerve innervates all of the extraocular muscles.
The oculomotor nerve innervates the dilator pupillae muscle.
The oculomotor nerve passes through the lateral part of the cavernous sinus.
The oculomotor nerve enters the orbit through the optic canal.
warnings: Source page and external anatomy reference reviewed; remains an unapproved OCR draft.
after.explanation: The oculomotor nerve travels in the lateral wall of the cavernous sinus and enters the orbit via the superior orbital fissure. It is a motor nerve and supplies sphincter pupillae through parasympathetic fibres, not dilator pupillae.
after.learningNote: The oculomotor nerve travels in the lateral wall of the cavernous sinus and enters the orbit via the superior orbital fissure. It is a motor nerve and supplies sphincter pupillae through parasympathetic fibres, not dilator pupillae.
after.highYieldNote: The oculomotor nerve travels in the lateral wall of the cavernous sinus and enters the orbit via the superior orbital fissure. It is a motor nerve and supplies sphincter pupillae through parasympathetic fibres, not dilator pupillae.
after.mnemonic: III is motor, travels in the cavernous sinus, and enters through SOF.

memoryAid.coreFact: The oculomotor nerve travels in the lateral wall of the cavernous sinus and enters the orbit via the superior orbital fissure. It is a motor nerve and supplies sphincter pupillae through parasympathetic fibres, not dilator pupillae.
memoryAid.mnemonic: III is motor, travels in the cavernous sinus, and enters through SOF.

before.stem: w A 29 year old man has sustained a significant head injury. On examination it is noted that his uvula is deviated to the right. Which of the following nerves is most likely affected:
options: Right glossopharyngeal nerve & Left glossopharyngeal nerve 1%
before.explanation: In damage to the vagus nerve, there is paralysis of the soft palate with deviation of the uvula away from the affected side. This is because the vagus nerve innervates the musculus uvulae muscle that makes up the core of the uvula. If only one side is effectively innervated, contraction of the active muscle will pull the uvula towards it. } Vv

after.stem: A 29 year old man has sustained a significant head injury. On examination it is noted that his uvula is deviated to the right. Which of the following nerves is most likely affected:
warnings: Source page and external anatomy reference reviewed; remains an unapproved OCR draft.
after.explanation: A unilateral vagus lesion causes the uvula to deviate away from the affected side. With left vagal weakness, the intact right side pulls the uvula rightward.
after.learningNote: A unilateral vagus lesion causes the uvula to deviate away from the affected side. With left vagal weakness, the intact right side pulls the uvula rightward.
after.highYieldNote: A unilateral vagus lesion causes the uvula to deviate away from the affected side. With left vagal weakness, the intact right side pulls the uvula rightward.
after.mnemonic: Vagus weakness pulls the uvula away: left lesion, right deviation.

memoryAid.coreFact: A unilateral vagus lesion causes the uvula to deviate away from the affected side. With left vagal weakness, the intact right side pulls the uvula rightward.
